findings_to_judge.finding: On 2026-08-12 Gamehaus said it will 'progressively optimize its third-party publishing business in casual titles, and in particular in the social casino category' and manage the existing portfolio 'on a cash flow- and profitability-oriented basis, with user acquisition and operating expenditure allocated according to return on investment rather than scale of installed base' - and that 'This approach took effect during the current quarter', i.e. the July-September quarter now in progress, which is exactly the quarter for which the 2026-09-08 release will issue its forward revenue guide.

Three separate structural events sit unabsorbed in front of the print: a $200,000,000 mixed-securities F-3 shelf filed 2026-07-28 and declared effective 2026-08-12 (about 4.5x the ~$44m market cap, with no prospectus supplement drawn as of 2026-09-04), a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency letter dated 2026-07-10 with a 2027-01-06 compliance deadline and no committed remedy, and a 2026-07-10 extraordinary general meeting that raised Class B voting power from 15 to 50 votes per share - control-proofing the founder immediately before an effective shelf.

The $5m buyback that caused a +105% single-day move when announced on 2025-08-28/30 was 88% unused when it expired: the 2026-08-28 6-K discloses only about 518,063 Class A shares repurchased for roughly $600,000 (an average near $1.16), meaning the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67, and then extended the same authorisation unchanged to 2027-08-28.

The baseline's 20-day average volume of 405,662 shares is essentially one session: GMHS traded 7,142,358 shares on 2026-08-31 (+16.51%) with no company filing or press release on or around that date, while the surrounding sessions traded 6,192 (2026-08-13), 19,279 (2026-08-11), 22,908 (2026-08-12), 35,144 (2026-08-27) and 66,901 (2026-08-28) shares - so the true book into this print is tens of thousands of shares a day, and the +16.5% spike has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77.
